items.claim: NIST released AI RMF 1.0 in January 2023.
items.synthesisExcerpt: NIST released AI RMF 1.0 in January 2023.
items.sourceEvidence: NIST released AI RMF 1.0 in January 2023.
items.usefulness: Establishes the broad framework's place in the timeline.

items.claim: AI RMF 1.0 is voluntary and aims to help organizations bring trustworthiness considerations into AI activities.
items.synthesisExcerpt: It was designed for voluntary use and aims to help organizations bring trustworthiness considerations into the design, development, use and evaluation of AI.
items.sourceEvidence: It was designed for voluntary use and aims to help organizations bring trustworthiness considerations into the design, development, use and evaluation of AI.
items.usefulness: Describes the framework's intended use and scope of guidance.
items.qualification: The stated aim is not a compliance requirement.

items.claim: NIST published AI 600-1 in July 2024 as a cross-sector companion profile for generative AI.
items.synthesisExcerpt: In July 2024 NIST published AI 600-1, a companion profile for generative AI with cross-sector scope.
items.sourceEvidence: In July 2024 NIST published AI 600-1, a companion profile for generative AI with cross-sector scope.
items.usefulness: Identifies the later, more focused document and its scope.
items.qualification: The source calls it a companion profile; it does not establish that it replaces AI RMF 1.0.

items.claim: AI 600-1 was prepared pursuant to Executive Order 14110.
items.synthesisExcerpt: The publication was prepared pursuant to Executive Order 14110.
items.sourceEvidence: The publication was prepared pursuant to Executive Order 14110.
items.usefulness: Provides context for the profile's development.
items.qualification: This attribution does not establish a private-sector compliance mandate.

items.claim: The publication's relation to Executive Order 14110 concerns its development, and the abstract does not describe mandatory private-sector compliance.
items.synthesisExcerpt: Its relation to the order concerns development of the publication; the abstract does not describe mandatory private-sector compliance.
items.sourceEvidence: Its relation to the order concerns development of the publication; the abstract does not describe mandatory private-sector compliance.
items.usefulness: Keeps the Executive Order attribution from being overstated.
items.qualification: Limited to what this abstract describes.

endpoint: The evidence supports a timeline from the broad AI RMF to a generative-AI companion profile, with their relationship framed as complementary guidance.
limitations: The synthesis does not establish that AI 600-1 replaces AI RMF 1.0.
The Executive Order attribution does not establish mandatory private-sector compliance.
